name: pong-loop
description: A 4-frame Pong rally where animation is pure geometry: a static field (dashed centre line + two paddles) on one layer, and a ball that bounces left-right-and-back on its own layer so the timing reads as eased motion. The forward loop closes because frame 3 leads cleanly back into frame 0.

steps.note: 32x24 court — wide enough that the ball's left-to-right travel reads as motion, short enough that 8x export stays a thumbnail-sized GIF.

Ball gets its own layer (index 1) above the field (layer 0). Keeping it separate is the whole trick: doc_anim_audit can then read JUST the ball's silhouette centre per frame, instead of the full composite whose bbox the static paddles would pin in place.

The whole static field in one batch: near-black ground, then THREE greens — a dark green dashed centre line (four 1x3 dashes), and a mid-green 2x6 paddle hugging each wall (left at x1-2, right at x29-30), both vertically centred on rows 9-14. This layer never changes again, so paddles stay pixel-crisp across the loop.
Frame 0: the bright-green 2x2 ball just off the left paddle (cols 4-5, centre row). This is the rally's start and end pose — its position is what the closed loop must return to.
Frame 1, duplicated from frame 0 (copies BOTH layers, so the field comes along free). We only have to move the ball; the court is already correct.
Frame 2, same duplicate-from-0 so it inherits the intact field.
Frame 3, the fourth and last frame; four frames total now exist so the per-frame edits below have somewhere to land.
Frame 1: erase the copied ball from its frame-0 spot on the ball layer only — the field underneath is untouched, so no stale ball ghosts onto the court.
Ball jumps from x4 to x18 — a big +14 step. This is mid-flight, away from both paddles, so it moves fastest here (the easing: long strides in the open court).

Frame 2: clear the inherited ball — every frame was copied from frame 0, so the stale ball sits at x4-5 here, NOT at frame 1's x18. Clear the real source position before repainting, or two balls would linger.
Ball reaches x26, a 1px gap from the right paddle (x29) — the bounce point. Only a +8 step this time: it decelerates as it nears the wall (ease-out into the paddle).
Frame 3: same again — this frame was also copied from frame 0, so its stale ball is at x4-5. Clear there before repainting on the return leg.

Ball rebounds left to x12 — a -14 step, fast again in open court. This sets up the wrap: frame 3 (x12) back to frame 0 (x4) is a -8 step, decelerating into the LEFT paddle exactly mirroring the right-side ease-out, so the forward loop closes symmetrically.

Sanity check: diff the ball layer between frame 0 and 1. Expect only ball pixels removed at x4-5 and added at x18-19 (the grid should show a clean -/+ pair and nothing on the field), proving the field stayed put and only the ball moved.

Tag all four frames as the 'rally' loop, played forward. Forward (not pingpong) is correct because the ball already returns toward its start within the four frames — the geometry itself carries the bounce.

The animator's timing chart for the ball layer: per_frame_center marches x 4.5 -> 18.5 -> 26.5 -> 12.5, and per_frame_offset reads +14, +8, -14 along x (the closing wrap 12.5 -> 4.5 is -8). The non-zero evenness is the eased motion made measurable — long strides (14) in the open court, short ones (8) braking into a paddle.
Render the rally tag to an 8x GIF so the 32x24 court is legible. This is the payoff: a crisp Pong loop built from nothing but rectangles moved on a timeline.
